did_you_know.text: Did you know? David assembled in Jerusalem not only the leaders of the tribes, but also the commanders of the divisions, the commanders of thousands and hundreds, the officials over the king’s and his sons’ possessions, the mighty warriors, and all the men of valor.
Did you know? David said that he had wanted to build a place of rest for the Ark of the Covenant of the Lord, and that he had also made preparations for himself and the people for its construction.
Did you know? According to David, the Lord did not allow him to build the house for His name because he was a man of war and had shed blood.
Did you know? David described his selection as king as a gradual process: the Lord chose Judah, then David’s father’s family, and finally David himself from among all his father’s sons.
Did you know? Although David had many sons, the Lord chose Solomon to sit on the throne of the Lord’s kingdom and to build the Temple.
Did you know? Solomon’s kingdom is described as being intended to last forever, but David states an explicit condition: Solomon must be strong and keep the Lord’s commandments and laws.
Did you know? David instructed Solomon to serve the Lord with a whole heart and a willing spirit, emphasizing that the Lord examines hearts and understands the inclination of their thoughts.
Did you know? David gave Solomon a detailed plan of the Temple, including the vestibule, the buildings, the storerooms, the upper rooms, the inner chambers, and the room of the Ark’s cover.
Did you know? The Temple plan also included precise weight specifications for the gold and silver used for the utensils, lampstands, tables, sacred vessels, the incense altar, and the cherubim.

Did you know? David said that all the details of the plan had been given to him in writing by the hand of the Lord, and that He had given him understanding for all the work described in the plan. He then encouraged Solomon to be strong, because the Lord would be with him until the work was completed.
